subject: MedixHealth VPC: performance remediation playbook and exec summary
messages:
From: Nora Chan <nora.chan@medixhealth.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@medixhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Sudden throughput drop + 500s from private VPC (production)

Rishi / Monica —

We started seeing elevated 5xx rates and a sustained throughput drop on our Medix private cluster at ~08:45 PT this morning. Error rate climbed to ~6% over a 30m window, p50 latency doubled, and several timeouts hit our front-end circuit breakers. Attaching the customer-side logs and a short trace sample.

Current impact:
- Primary inference path returning HTTP 500s during heavy batch windows (08:45–09:30).
- Background batch jobs retrying and saturating GPU host I/O.
- User-facing page load errors for a subset of requests.

Can Redwood confirm root cause and an ETA for mitigation? This is production traffic — we need an action plan and a timeline.

Nora
VP Eng, MedixHealth

Attachments: request_logs_1100-1400.jsonl (10MB)

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: Nora Chan <nora.chan@medixhealth.com>, Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@medixhealth.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput drop + 500s from private VPC (production)

Nora — thank you for the signal and the logs. We’ve triaged and started live capture. Quick summary of immediate steps we are taking:

1) Isolation: routing portion of Medix traffic to a cold standby pool to reduce pressure and get a clean failure window (5–10m work).
2) Trace collection: our infra agent is collecting per-host kernel and GPU metrics and full KV cache stats.
3) Short-term mitigation: if IO saturation is confirmed we will temporarily reduce concurrent batch sizes and disable high-concurrency retriers for the next 30m.

I’m looping Monica (customer lead) and Stephanie (runtime infra) + Vivek (kernel/runtime tuning) for deeper analysis and a remediation playbook. I’ll send a concise exec summary for your leadership and propose a maintenance window if needed.

ETA for first mitigation changes: ~20–30 minutes, I’ll update.

—Rishi
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: flamegraph_20261130.png

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, Nora Chan <nora.chan@medixhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput drop + 500s from private VPC (production)

Quick findings from the first 30m of captures:

- Symptom: a subset of hosts show elevated kernel scheduling contention correlated with long-running GC-like spikes in the Python worker processes. When these GC events overlap with large batch KV cache misses, we observe request-time cross-host stalls and backend 500s.
- Evidence: I’ve attached a flamegraph highlight (flamegraph_20261130.png) and the request-level logs that show retries spiking.

Initial remediation steps (short window, low risk):
- Reduce per-worker concurrent batches from 8 -> 4 on the impacted pool. (Config change + hot-reload, no restart required.)
- Disable aggressive retrier logic for 10 minutes to avoid request amplification.
- Increase KV cache prefetch window on hosts with under-utilized GPU memory to reduce cache miss rate.

If these steps stabilize the cluster we can schedule a low-risk rolling restart with a small kernel parameter tweak (see medix_vpc_kerneltune_diff.patch) to avoid recurring scheduling contention.

Request: Vivek — can you validate the kernel parameter(s) in the patch and whether a rolling restart is required?

-Stephanie
Runtime/Infra

Attachments: medix_vpc_kerneltune_diff.patch, flamegraph_20261130.png

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput drop + 500s from private VPC (production)

Reviewed the patch. Short summary:
- Root cause hypothesis: host-level scheduler preemption + high page cache churn when concurrent batches align with heavy background snapshot/backup I/O. That combination manifests as long tail pauses in user-space workers.
- medix_vpc_kerneltune_diff.patch proposes: tune kernel scheduler latency ns, increase swappiness threshold for inference hosts, and pin the realtime infer threads to a restricted CPU set. These are safe with a brief rolling restart.

Operational plan (recommended):
1) Apply the config change to 1 host in the impacted pool during a quick maintenance slot (5–10min window) and monitor.
2) If metrics improve, perform staged rolling restarts across the pool with 10m ramp per host.
3) Post-change, run a short stress harness (we have a copy of Medix dev load) to validate latency distribution.

Risk: low-to-moderate. We will preserve the standby routing fallback and can rollback the patch quickly.

I’ll stand by for Monica to approve scheduling.

—Vivek
Kernel & Performance Engineering

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: monica_patel@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: Nora Chan <nora.chan@medixhealth.com>, Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@medixhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: MedixHealth VPC performance - exec summary and recommended maintenance window

Monica — high-level executive note for approval (copying customer):

Summary: Production VPC for MedixHealth experienced elevated 5xxs and a throughput regression due to host-level scheduling contention overlapping with KV cache misses. Stephanie and Vivek recommend a low-risk kernel parameter change + staged rolling restarts. Short mitigations (reduce batch concurrency, disable retriers) have already been applied and are stabilizing traffic.

Proposed immediate action:
- Maintenance window: Tue 2026-12-01 02:00–03:00 PT (low traffic window for Medix).
- Scope: apply medix_vpc_kerneltune_diff.patch to impacted pool via staged rolling restarts (10m per host), run smoke harness after each restart.
- Customer impact: transient connection re-routes for ~1–2% of traffic during roll. We will coordinate with Medix to throttle test runs and enable standby pool routing.
- Post-change deliverables: short exec one-pager, metric comparison (p50/p95/error rate), and remediation runbook.

Decision requested: Monica, please confirm approval for the maintenance window and SLA credit guidance if we need to offer a goodwill adjustment.

Thanks — I’ll prepare the runbook and notify Medix once we have approval.

—Rishi

From: monica_patel@redwood.com
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: Nora Chan <nora.chan@medixhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 13:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: MedixHealth VPC performance - exec summary and recommended maintenance window

Approved. Proceed with the maintenance window on Tue 02:00–03:00 PT. Please ensure all of the following before starting:
- Postmortem owner assigned (Rishi) and an exec one-pager drafted and shared to the customer before EOD Wed.
- Customer comms template prepared (Nora, please confirm); include rollback criteria and a contact tree.
- If we need to offer a credit, limit to a goodwill SLA credit (pre-approval for up to 5% monthly credit) and get Legal looped if Finance needs a formal adjustment.

Also, surface how long we expect the change to hold (30-day observation suggested).

-Monica
VP Customer Success

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: monica_patel@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, Nora Chan <nora.chan@medixhealth.com>, Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@medixhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 17:45:00 -0800
Subject: MedixHealth VPC remediation: completed patch runbook & next steps

Update: the rolling changes were executed as planned during the 02:00 PT window. Outcome summary:
- All restarts completed within target; p50 returned to baseline and p95 improved ~18% versus pre-change. Error rate reduced from ~6% -> 0.8% in the first 3h post-change.
- We executed staged stress runs (links below) and saw no regression in throughput at the configured batch sizes.

Deliverables uploaded:
- Postmortem one-pager: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bMedixPerformance (see file "Medix_executive_one_pager_20261201.pdf")
- Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RI-2148 (contains remediation checklist + rollback steps)
- Attachments: medix_vpc_kerneltune_diff.patch, flamegraph_20261130.png, request_logs_1100-1400.jsonl

Next steps / monitoring:
- 30-day observation window with daily health ping to Medix and automated regression alerts for p95 or error rate >1.5%.
- Schedule follow-up tuning meeting w/ customer next week to review batch sizing and quantization tradeoffs.

Thanks to the oncall and infra teams for the quick turnaround. Nora — please let me know if you want a short post-change walkthrough tomorrow morning.

—Rishi
Sr. Solutions Engineer
